publisher_assessment.publisher: Alþingi (Icelandic Parliament) and official public authorities
publisher_assessment.decision: Accept the listed government-published links for their stated, limited uses. The current Alþingi consolidated-law pages are accepted as external references in Icelandic.
publisher_assessment.basis: The publisher and instrument identities are clear. Alþingi current law pages display Lagasafn edition 158a dated 1 October 2026. The official Ministry of Justice immigration page links to Alþingi, Reglugerðasafn and published appeal decisions. The Courts Administration publishes Rules No. 3/2022 on its official court-service network and identifies its effective date and repeal of the 2019 rule. The official Directorate of Immigration processing page was checked on 24 October 2026 and states that its selected-type averages are based on applications approved so far in the year and do not predict an individual pending decision. Alþingi’s current consolidated Visa Act No. 37/2026 page identifies edition 158a dated 1 October 2026 and an effective date of 12 May 2026.
publisher_assessment.limitation: All accepted external references retain their recorded narrow scopes. Nine locally maintained English summaries are accepted (is-05 and is-08 through is-17 as selected: is-08, is-09, is-10, is-11, is-13, is-14, is-16 and is-17); none is a full statutory text. No topics are accepted and the Iceland review remains incomplete. The linked Regulation 540/2017 base text predates listed amendments 669/2026, 724/2026 and 725/2026. The registration threshold conflict remains unresolved; court and appeals publications are not established as exhaustive.

completion_note: Thirty-six official external references have scoped acceptance. Nine maintained source summaries are accepted (is-05, is-08, is-09, is-10, is-11, is-13, is-14, is-16 and is-17); no local full statutory text or topic is accepted, and Iceland is not complete. Open work includes resolving the three-month/six-month registration guidance conflict against primary law, verifying court-search coverage and continuing case-law discovery, mapping visa and immigration judicial remedies, checking current mission instructions, and completing operational and dependency review.
